references.text: Prohibition against erecting sacred pillars and stone images as objects of worship, demonstrating God's abhorrence of such practices.
Command to break down the stone pillars of the Canaanite peoples, emphasizing Israel's prohibition against adopting pagan forms of worship.
Instruction to tear down pagan altars and smash stone pillars, showing that such objects are incompatible with the worship of the Lord.
Directive to dismantle the altars and stone pillars of the Canaanites as part of the cleansing of the land.
Command to destroy pagan places of worship, including stone pillars, before the Israelites establish their own worship.
During Rehoboam's reign, Judah erected stone pillars in violation of God's command, leading to sin and apostasy.
Description of how the high places and stone pillars persisted during Joash's time, despite the prohibition.
King Hezekiah removed the stone pillars as part of his religious reform, in obedience to God's command.
Prophetic judgment against Israel that it shall be without a sacred pillar, indicating both the loss of false worship and legitimate service.
The Lord will destroy the stone pillars from among Israel, as part of the judgment on idolatry.
